# Provider and model capability reference

Generated from the descriptors in code, not hand copied. If this file and
the code disagree, the build fails rather than the file quietly aging.

## Capability evidence is tri-state

Every capability below is `Supported`, `Unsupported`, or `Unknown`, and the
three are different claims:

| Value | Rendered | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Supported` | `yes` | The provider or model explicitly supports it. |
| `Unsupported` | `no` | The provider or model explicitly does not. |
| `Unknown` | `unknown` | No trustworthy evidence yet. This is **not** a synonym for "no". |

`Unknown` never becomes `Supported` by inference. A capability is marked
supported because a provider evidenced it, not because a similar model has it
or because the name suggests it.

One nuance that has come up repeatedly and is easy to get backwards: a
**gateway-provided** capability may legitimately be marked supported by the
layer that provides it — a router that documents fallback web search for any
model can honour that claim whatever the upstream model does. A
**model-intrinsic** capability, such as image input, cannot be supplied by any
layer below the model, so no gateway's documentation can evidence it.

## Providers

Knowing a provider is not the same as being able to send it a request. A
provider marked `configured only` ships a profile, a catalog, or an
authorization flow, but direct inference is unavailable, so it cannot be
selected as `[llm] provider`. Z.ai Coding Plan restricts usage to officially
supported tools; heycode is not listed. Use the separate general API route
with its own key. See <https://docs.z.ai/devpack/usage-policy>.

| Provider | Route |
| --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | inference |
| `azure-openai` | inference |
| `bedrock` | inference |
| `bedrock-mantle` | inference |
| `custom-openai` | inference |

## Per-model capability data is live, and is not in this file

Model lists and their capability snapshots come from each provider's
`ModelCatalog::fetch`, which is a network call against the provider's own
model-listing endpoint and usually needs a credential. A table of models
checked in here would state one machine's cache as though it were a fact
about heycode, and could not be regenerated in CI.

To see the live capability data for the models you can actually reach, use
the model picker or the catalog surfaces in the running application. A model
absent from a live catalog is described by a conservative descriptor whose
every capability is `Unknown` — again, not `Unsupported`.
